rubrics.justification: The response correctly identifies a blastocyst and notes zona thinning/expansion consistent with the provided 3AA label, but it overstates confidence in visible ICM and TE quality from this single low-contrast image. Some described features (compact A-grade ICM, fairly continuous A-grade TE, no collapse artifact) are not clearly discernible.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, endometrial thickness, prior IVF outcomes, semen parameters, BMI, and lifestyle well, and appropriately relates these to embryo prognosis and transfer planning.

The reasoning is structured and internally consistent overall, with conclusions generally supported by the case data. Minor issues include somewhat speculative discussion of protocol alternatives and low oocyte yield without enough context.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET for a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, attention to hydrosalpinx, standard luteal support, and selective rather than routine PGT-A at age 24. Slight overreach appears in protocol commentary and precise success estimates.

Provides clear practical next steps for the current transfer and contingency planning if unsuccessful, including SET, hydrosalpinx exclusion, luteal support review, uterine cavity assessment, and future stimulation considerations.
